findings.title: God class: DataOfficerService implements 10 sub-modules in 1054 LOC with 14 injected repositories
findings.cvss: Maintainability risk: a 1054-LOC class with 14 collaborators and 10 distinct domains is the single highest-churn merge-conflict hotspot in the module; every DSR/Consent/DPIA/Breach/Notice/Retention/NDR/Catalog/Quality/Ethics change touches it.
findings.description: DataOfficerService is a single @Service that owns the full lifecycle of ten unrelated PDPL/NDMO sub-modules (DSR, Consent, DPIA, Breach, Privacy Notice, Retention/Disposal, NDR, Catalog/Lineage, Quality, Ethics). It declares 7 state-machine maps, injects 14 repositories + 1 event publisher (lines 120-134), and contains ~30 public methods and ~13 static mapper methods. This is a textbook Single-Responsibility violation: the class has ten reasons to change.
findings.rootCause: All ten sub-modules were placed in one class to 'share a single tenant-scoped event timeline and a consistent state-machine validator' (class Javadoc, lines 24-44). The shared infrastructure (timeline/emit/validate) does not require co-location of the ten domains.
findings.evidence: 1054 LOC (wc -l). 14 `private final ...Repository` fields (lines 120-133) plus ApplicationEventPublisher (134). 7 static transition maps DSR_ALLOWED..ETHICS_ALLOWED (lines 52-118). Sub-modules numbered 1..10 in section banners.
findings.impact: High coupling and low cohesion: any change to one regulatory surface forces recompilation/retesting of the whole class and maximises merge conflicts across teams. Unit testing requires mocking all 14 repositories even to exercise one path.
findings.reproduction: Open the file; observe section banners '1. DSR' (136) through '10. Ethics' (697) and the 14-field constructor block (120-134).
findings.resolution: Extract one @Service per sub-module (DsrService, ConsentService, DpiaService, ...), each injecting only its own repository. Hoist the shared timeline/emit/validate/org/currentUserId helpers into a single injectable collaborator (e.g. DataOfficerTimeline / a common base), and keep the dashboard aggregation in a thin DashboardService that fans out to the sub-services.
references: Robert C. Martin, Clean Code, ch.10 (Classes)

findings.title: Copy-pasted tenant/event helpers (currentUserId, emit, validate, org) duplicated verbatim across services
findings.cvss: Maintainability: identical helper blocks in 3+ target-module services (18 codebase-wide for currentUserId) mean a security/semantic fix to the principal-extraction or event-emit logic must be applied in every copy or it silently diverges.
findings.description: The helper quartet validate(Map,from,to,label), emit(trigger,entityType,entityId,payload), org(), and currentUserId() is duplicated byte-for-byte across DataOfficerService, DataclassService and AiLifecycleService (and the per-entity timeline() differs only in which event entity it builds). jscpd flags AiLifecycleService:335-363 as a clone of DataclassService:383-408 and DataOfficerService:886-910, and the same block recurs in OutsourcingService, RegInspectService, OpResService, FraudService.
findings.rootCause: No shared base class or injectable helper for the common multi-tenant + domain-event plumbing; each sprint copied the pattern into a new service.
findings.evidence: grep for the exact line `auth.getPrincipal() instanceof GrcUserDetails u)) return null` matches 3 target-module services; `private static Long currentUserId() {` appears in 18 files codebase-wide. The `emit(...)` DomainEvent builder appears in 4 files. jscpd top hit: 29-line clone AiLifecycleService.java:335-363 <-> DataclassService.java:383-408.
findings.impact: A change to principal resolution (e.g. handling a new GrcUserDetails subtype) or to the DomainEvent constructor signature must be made in every copy; missing one produces silent behavioural drift across modules.
findings.reproduction: Diff DataclassService lines 392-406 against DataOfficerService lines 896-912 — identical apart from whitespace.
findings.resolution: Introduce a shared component (e.g. TenantActor / DomainEventEmitter) exposing org(), currentUserId(), emit(...) and validate(...); inject it into each service. Keep only the entity-specific timeline() row construction local.

findings.title: Swallowed exceptions: NdiAuditPublisher catches Exception and discards it with no logging
findings.cvss: Operational risk: three write paths and currentUsername() swallow every exception with `catch (Exception ignored)` and no log statement, so audit-ledger write failures vanish silently — directly undermining the compliance value of the audit trail this class exists to populate.
findings.description: publishTransition (40), publish (49) and publish-with-severity (60) each wrap the repo.save in `catch (Exception ignored) { /* swallow */ }`, and currentUsername() (82) does the same. The class Javadoc claims errors are 'intentionally swallowed at warn level' (lines 19-22) but there is NO Logger field and NO warn/error call anywhere in the file — the comment is false and the failures are completely invisible.
findings.rootCause: Deliberate decision to never let an audit failure roll back the parent op (REQUIRES_NEW propagation), but implemented as a blind swallow rather than a logged swallow; the documenting comment was never reconciled with the code.
findings.evidence: Lines 40, 49, 60, 82 all contain `catch (Exception ignored)`. No `Logger`/`LoggerFactory` import in the file. Javadoc lines 19-22 promise 'warn level' logging that does not exist.
findings.impact: If the audit table is unavailable, schema-drifted, or a summary exceeds a constraint, NDI compliance/maturity/submission transitions still succeed but their audit rows silently disappear — an undetectable gap in the regulatory ledger and no signal to operators.
findings.reproduction: Force NdiAuditEventRepository.save to throw (e.g. drop the table in a test); call any NDI transition — the operation succeeds and nothing is logged.
findings.resolution: Add a SLF4J Logger and log at WARN with the full exception (cause) in each catch, matching the Javadoc's stated contract; keep the swallow so the parent op is unaffected.
findings.patchBefore: } catch (Exception ignored) { /* audit failure never rolls back the parent op */ }
references: CWE-390: Detection of Error Condition Without Action

findings.title: Hand-rolled JSON serializer and Markdown→HTML converter in ReportComposerService reinvent Jackson
findings.cvss: Correctness + maintainability: a bespoke recursive toJson() (lines 461-487) silently mishandles types Jackson handles (no LocalDate/BigDecimal-as-number coercion, no Map-key escaping, dates only stringified upstream) and markdownToHtml() does O(n) `out.toString()` scans per cell, while Jackson is already a project dependency injected into peer services.
findings.description: toJson(Object) (461-487) is a hand-written recursive JSON encoder; the comment at 459-460 explicitly says 'pulling Jackson isn't necessary'. Meanwhile NdiSubmissionPackageService and NdiReportService inject a Spring-managed ObjectMapper for exactly this. The encoder does not escape Map keys, only escapes a subset of control characters in strings, and renders any non-Map/Iterable/Number/Boolean (e.g. LocalDate, enum) via toString() with only quote-escaping. markdownToHtml (409-450) determines table-header vs cell by calling `out.toString().endsWith(...)` inside the per-cell loop (lines 424) — re-materialising the entire growing buffer on every cell.
findings.rootCause: Author chose a local mini-implementation over the existing Jackson bean to avoid a perceived dependency, and a string-scan heuristic over tracking parser state in a variable.
findings.evidence: Line 459-460 comment: 'Quick JSON serializer — service is small enough that pulling Jackson isn't necessary'. Line 424: `boolean isHeader = !out.toString().endsWith("</tr>") && out.toString().endsWith("<table><tr>");` — two full-buffer scans per cell. 14 injected fields (grep -c 'private final' = 14) but no ObjectMapper.
findings.impact: Risk of malformed JSON in exported BOARD_ESG/CMA/GHG report bundles when a value is a date/enum/Map-with-special-key; quadratic-ish HTML rendering for large GHG/evidence tables; divergence from how every other report service serialises.
findings.reproduction: Pass a Map whose value is a LocalDate into the JSON path (e.g. via dashboard 'overall') — it is emitted as a quoted toString, not the canonical Jackson form; build a GHG report with 1000 records and profile markdownToHtml.
findings.resolution: Inject the existing ObjectMapper bean and call writeValueAsString for the JSON branch; for markdownToHtml track header-state in a local boolean (firstRowOfTable) instead of scanning out.toString(). Optionally replace with a maintained Markdown library.
references: Effective Java, Item 59: Know and use the libraries

findings.title: Long high-branching method: suggestWorkflowSubmissionReview spans 120 LOC with a 7-way if/else ladder
findings.cvss: Maintainability: a single method building seven near-identical bilingual checklist blocks via a long if/else-if chain on substring matches is hard to extend (each new wizard adds another branch) and hard to test in isolation.
findings.description: suggestWorkflowSubmissionReview is 120 LOC. The body is a 7-branch if/else-if ladder (workflowId.contains('pdpl-breach') ... else generic, lines 307-392), each branch pushing 4 English + 4 Arabic strings into two lists and setting headline/decision/conf, followed by a second status-dependent if/else (395-397). Cyclomatic complexity is roughly 12+ from the chained predicates.
findings.rootCause: Per-wizard checklist content is hard-coded inline as procedural branches rather than data-driven (a lookup table keyed by workflowId/module).
findings.evidence: Method line span 291-411 = 120 lines. Branch conditions at 307, 320, 333, 345, 357, 369, 379 (else), plus status branches at 395-397.
findings.impact: Every new wizard type requires editing this method and re-testing the whole ladder; the bilingual string pairs are easy to desynchronise (EN added without AR). The method mixes content definition with persistence (calls persist() at the end).
findings.reproduction: Open the method; count the else-if branches from line 307 to 392.
findings.resolution: Move the per-wizard content into a static Map<String, ReviewTemplate> (or a small enum/record table) keyed by workflowId-prefix/module; the method then becomes a lookup + a default, dropping branch complexity to ~2.
references: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism / table-driven design

findings.title: Repetitive synthesizer boilerplate: 12 near-identical row-mapping methods in NdiReportService
findings.cvss: Maintainability: 12 private synthesizer methods (184-436) each repeat the same LinkedHashMap-build + stream-map-row + ReportResult-wrap shape, so a change to the result envelope or row convention must be replicated 12 times.
findings.description: executiveSummary, maturityHeatmap, complianceStatus, opexDashboard, gapRegister, capaRegister, roadmap, evidenceInventory, domainRollup, cycleHistory, auditTrail, submissionExport all follow the same template: build a summary LinkedHashMap, map a row list with `Map<String,Object> row = new LinkedHashMap<>(); row.put(...); return row;`, and wrap in a ReportResult. The per-field row.put blocks (e.g. 215-222, 235-244, 257-267) are structurally identical and only differ in the entity getters.
findings.rootCause: No generic row-projection helper; each report type was authored independently.
findings.evidence: Pattern `Map<String, Object> row = new LinkedHashMap<>();` followed by N row.put(...) calls appears in 10 of the 12 synthesizers. dispatch switch at 165-179 routes to all of them.
findings.impact: Adding a column convention (e.g. always include 'id') or changing ReportResult shape is a 12-site edit; high copy-paste surface invites inconsistency between report types.
findings.reproduction: Compare maturityHeatmap (207-225) and complianceStatus (227-247) — same skeleton, different getters.
findings.resolution: Extract a small generic helper `rows(List<T> src, Function<T, Map<String,Object>> projector)` and a `result(type, cycleId, summary, rows)` factory so each synthesizer reduces to a projector lambda; or drive projection from a column-definition map.
findings.patchAfter:
return result("MATURITY_HEATMAP", cycleId, sum, project(rows, m -> Map.of(
    "id", m.getId(), "domain", m.getDomain(), "currentLevel", m.getCurrentLevel(), ...)));

findings.title: Injected-but-unused ObjectMapper field flagged with @SuppressWarnings instead of removed
findings.cvss: Minor: a constructor-injected dependency that is never used is dead weight that misleads readers about the class's collaborators and was deliberately masked with @SuppressWarnings rather than removed.
findings.description: Field `@SuppressWarnings("unused") private final ObjectMapper json;` (line 58) is injected through the constructor (param at 71, assigned at 83) but never referenced anywhere in the class body. The @SuppressWarnings annotation acknowledges the dead dependency rather than removing it.
findings.rootCause: Likely a leftover from an earlier design where the report service serialised JSON itself; the field was retained 'just in case' and silenced.
findings.evidence: Line 58 declaration carries @SuppressWarnings("unused"); grep for `json.` in the file returns no usages (only the assignment `this.json = json;` at line 83).
findings.impact: Misleading API surface and an unnecessary bean dependency; the suppression normalises leaving dead injected fields in place.
findings.reproduction: Search the file for `json.` — there are no method calls on the field.
findings.resolution: Remove the field, its constructor parameter, and the assignment. If JSON serialisation is planned, add it back when actually used.
findings.patchBefore:
@SuppressWarnings("unused") private final ObjectMapper json;
... NdiReportService(..., ObjectMapper json) { ...; this.json = json; }
findings.patchAfter: // field, constructor param, and assignment removed

findings.title: Per-instance new ObjectMapper() in AiSuggestionService instead of injecting the shared bean
findings.cvss: Minor: constructing a fresh ObjectMapper as a field initialiser ignores the Spring-managed, configured ObjectMapper used elsewhere (NdiReportService/NdiSubmissionPackageService inject it), so any project-wide Jackson config (modules, date handling) does not apply here.
findings.description: Line 35: `private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();` builds an un-configured mapper local to the service while the rest of the codebase autowires the Spring-configured ObjectMapper. The mapper is used in persist() (457-459) to serialise input/output payloads.
findings.rootCause: Inconsistent dependency strategy — this service self-instantiates Jackson rather than injecting the application bean.
findings.evidence: Line 35 `new ObjectMapper()`; compare NdiSubmissionPackageService line 60 / NdiReportService line 58 which take ObjectMapper via constructor injection.
findings.impact: If the application customises Jackson (e.g. JavaTimeModule, fail-on-unknown), AiSuggestion input/output JSON is serialised with default settings, diverging from other modules; also two divergent ObjectMapper configs in one app are a known footgun.
findings.reproduction: Add a global Jackson customiser and observe it is not reflected in AiSuggestion.outputJson.
findings.resolution: Inject ObjectMapper via the constructor (Lombok @RequiredArgsConstructor already in use) and drop the `new ObjectMapper()` initialiser.
findings.patchBefore: private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
findings.patchAfter: private final ObjectMapper mapper; // injected; @RequiredArgsConstructor wires the Spring bean

findings.title: Cross-tenant findAll() in NdiScheduler report loop and org-discovery shortcut
findings.cvss: Correctness/scalability: reportScheduleSweep iterates reportDefs.findAll() across every tenant each minute and distinctOrgIds() derives the tenant universe from the report-definition table, a self-admitted demo shortcut that loads all orgs' rows into memory.
findings.description: reportScheduleSweep (82) calls reportDefs.findAll() — a non-tenant-scoped query that pulls every organisation's report definitions every 60s. distinctOrgIds() (119-127) also calls findAll() and maps to distinct organisation ids to drive the evidence-expiry sweep. The class Javadoc (lines 34-41) explicitly notes this is a demo shortcut that 'in production a proper org-iteration service would replace'.
findings.rootCause: No platform-level tenant registry; the scheduler improvises tenant discovery from a domain table and bypasses the org-scoped repository finders the rest of the module uses.
findings.evidence: Line 84 `for (NdiReportDefinition def : reportDefs.findAll())`; lines 122-126 `reportDefs.findAll().stream().map(...).distinct().toList()`. Javadoc 34-41 documents the shortcut.
findings.impact: Memory + query cost grows linearly with all tenants' report definitions on every minute tick; tenants with no report definitions are invisible to the evidence-expiry sweep, so their evidence never auto-expires. Repository usage bypasses the org-scoped finder convention.
findings.reproduction: Add a tenant with NDI evidence but no report definitions; observe its evidence is never swept (distinctOrgIds omits it).
findings.resolution: Introduce a platform tenant-registry service and iterate that; or add a dedicated paged/streamed query keyed by 'has schedule cron' to avoid full-table scans. Decouple expiry-sweep org discovery from the report-definition table.
references: CLAUDE.md: 'Every repository query must filter by organisation_id'

findings.title: Inline fully-qualified type reference instead of an import in MlModelService
findings.cvss: Cosmetic: one collaborator is declared with its fully-qualified package path inline rather than an import, breaking the file's own convention and hurting readability.
findings.description: Field declaration `private final com.tss.grc.module.ai.governance.repository.MlModelAuditRepository auditRepo;` uses the fully-qualified class name inline while the sibling field `private final MlModelRepository repo;` (line 79) uses a normal import. The two are in the same package so the FQN is gratuitous.
findings.rootCause: Likely an IDE auto-complete that inserted the FQN; never normalised to an import.
findings.evidence: Line 80 contains the full package path; line 79 uses the short name for a repository in the same package.
findings.impact: Inconsistent style; marginally harder to scan the dependency list. No functional effect.
findings.resolution: Add `import com.tss.grc.module.ai.governance.repository.MlModelAuditRepository;` and use the short type name.
